identity.name: ROSSELL TECHSYS LIMITED
identity.industry: Aerospace & defence — build-to-print electrical/wiring systems & high-reliability EMS (wire harnesses, panels, interconnect)

summary.oneLiner: Niche build-to-print wire-harness/interconnect EMS supplier on "nearly every US military platform" that just nearly doubled revenue (FY26 INR485cr, +87%) and more-than-doubled PBT, while diversifying decisively beyond aerospace/defence into space (Amazon) and semiconductor-equipment harnesses. Visibility is unusually strong: ~INR715cr confirmed POs plus ~INR3,000cr of strategic agreements on top, with mgmt guiding to another ~80–90% revenue growth in FY27 and 17–22% EBITDA margins. Multiple optionalities (commercial aerospace entry, MRO licensing, US RTI build-out, content-share gains per platform) sit outside current numbers, funded by a planned QIP (7–10% dilution).

scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | YoY | FY26 | FY25 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (INR cr) | ~142 | ~88 | +62% | 485 | 259 | +87% |
| EBITDA (INR cr) | — | — | — | 66 | 38 | +74% |
| EBITDA margin | — | — | — | ~13.6% | ~14.7% | down |
| PBT (INR cr) | — | — | — | 28 | 10 | +180% |
| PAT (INR cr) | ~9.5 | — | — | — | — | — |
| Employee cost (% rev) | — | — | — | 15.5% | — | targeting lower |
| Inventory coverage (months) | — | — | — | 7.67 | ~10 | improved |
| Headcount | — | — | — | ~1,200 | (680 two yrs ago) | scaling |

Note: Q4 FY26 was "strongest quarter in company history." FY26 EBITDA margin (~13.6%) sits below mgmt's 17–22% structural range due to upfront investment/qualification (FAI) costs; margins were sequentially weaker — flagged by multiple analysts. Inventory grew only +45% vs +87% revenue.
guidance:
- FY27 revenue: another "similar" ~80–90% growth (vs +87% in FY26); mgmt declined a hard number. Prior 2-yr aspiration of ~INR1,300cr top line reiterated (FY26 did ~INR500cr; FY27 implicitly heading toward ~INR800cr+).
- FY27 revenue mix: ~50% aerospace & defence / ~50% non-A&D (space + semiconductor).
- Space + semiconductor each guided +300–400% YoY in FY27 (base: ~20% of FY26 revenue came from these two combined).
- EBITDA margin: structural 17–22% in current competencies; FY27 expected to improve vs FY26; MRO higher (services); phase-2 electromechanical assemblies (2028–29) could reach 21–30%.
- Semiconductor revenue potential ~US$200m in 3–5 years; T-7 strategic agreement ~US$200m.
- Inventory coverage targeted down from 7.67 months toward an eventual 4 months.
- Employee cost targeted below 15.5% of revenue.
order book:
- Confirmed POs ~INR715cr; FY26 order inflow ~INR570cr.
- Strategic agreements ~INR3,000cr — OVER AND ABOVE the INR715cr POs (mgmt explicitly confirmed). POs are placed against these 6–12 months before delivery; gives ~3-year visibility.
- Bids submitted during FY26 ~INR4,500cr across aerospace/defence/space/semiconductor.
- Landmark multi-year space contract ~INR400cr won during the year; repeat orders from overseas defence customers.
- T-7 (Boeing) strategic agreement ~US$200m; deliveries started, ramp from later FY27 (mgmt suggested Q2/Q3), then 5–7 years of growth.
- Confirmed-PO split ~50/50 A&D vs non-A&D; strategic agreements skew toward A&D.
- Legacy loss-making Boeing program: ~INR75cr executed in FY26, ~INR70cr remaining (front-loaded into H1 FY27).
segment: Aerospace & defence (core, build-to-print wire harnesses/panels for Boeing & US military platforms; on "nearly every US military platform"; long-term 5-yr contracts with back-to-back supplier agreements). Space (wire harnesses for Amazon — moved on from Blue Origin; first large production batches executed; scaling FY27; US RTI presence encouraged by a space customer). Semiconductor (wire harnesses for semicap equipment; qualified Q2 FY26, ramped immediately; new global top-tier semi customer being onboarded; ~50/50 weighting with space inside the non-A&D bucket). Commercial aerospace (currently Tier-2; shortlisted by OEMs re-shoring supply base to India; RFPs expected ~Q2 FY27; "transformational" optionality). MRO/aftermarket (DPL + AS9110 licenses now in place; marketing to existing + new customers, organic + inorganic; revenue pickup in coming quarters).
growth: Macro tailwinds: global commercial-aero production ramp, rising defence GDP spend, LEO/space ecosystem build-out, semiconductor-equipment capex with China+1 supply-base diversification into India, and supply-chain-resilience demand for "trusted manufacturing partners." Company-specific: high qualification barriers (moat), 300–400% growth in space & semi, content-share expansion ("X into 3 to 5") on existing platforms (phase-2, 2028+), commercial aerospace entry, MRO, and RTI US expansion. 98% of revenue exported (~80% North America; diversifying into Southeast Asia, Middle East, Europe).
margins: FY26 EBITDA ~13.6% (INR66cr on INR485cr), below mgmt's 17–22% structural band and sequentially weaker — repeatedly questioned by analysts. Cause: front-loaded investment in people, infrastructure, training, tooling, automation, and heavy first-article-inspection (FAI)/qualification spend for new space & semiconductor customers that generates no current-year revenue but drives repeat orders and higher margins later. Mgmt insists margins improve in FY27 and that semiconductor (despite high-volume) stays in the 17–22% band via automation. Back-to-back supplier contracts + EPA (equitable price adjustment) clauses + advance/upfront payments on long-lead single-source items mitigate raw-material and working-capital risk.
capex: Pivot from building a new facility to LEASING ~210,000 sq ft adjacent to existing operations — faster operational readiness; space & semiconductor programs migrate there; expected to deliver revenue comparable to the existing facility. Ensures capacity is not a growth constraint. Investing in automation, quality/testing infrastructure, planning & supply-chain systems, and VR-based workforce training. US RTI infrastructure being evaluated for expansion on customer demand.
capital allocation: Maiden dividend announced (quantum not specified on call). Planned QIP to raise ~7–10% (sized off market cap, 5% up/down band) — proceeds for (1) capacity expansion/facility footprint, (2) operational/quality/testing infrastructure, (3) working capital for scale & long-lead inventory; seeking "the right investor." Debt has risen with growth; multi-banking framework; additional working-capital facilities secured in Q4. Inventory-coverage reduction (7.67→4 months target) is the key self-funding lever. CFO acknowledged operating cash flow still negative, improvement expected over coming years.
risks:
- Margins running below the 17–22% guide; recovery hinges on qualifications converting to repeat volume.
- Negative operating cash flow and rising debt while scaling ~90%/yr — heavy working-capital intensity.
- Execution-dilutive QIP (7–10% dilution) and dependence on raising capital to fund growth.
- Customer concentration: Boeing in A&D, single large customer in each of space (Amazon) and semiconductor today.
- Legacy loss-making Boeing program (~INR70cr) still to run off in H1 FY27.
- Revenue 98% export / ~80% North America → FX, US tariff/policy and freight exposure (though customers pay freight, air-freighted, mostly CIF/customer-paid).
- Guidance is qualitative ("similar to last year"); space/semi 300–400% growth off a small base; commercial-aero entry still pre-RFP.
- Margin pressure if semiconductor volume mix dilutes blended profitability.
mgmt tone: Very bullish and promotional — "strongest quarter in history," "structurally higher growth trajectory," "sky's the limit," "designed to compound." MD candid on margin miss (attributes to investment/qualification, promises recovery) and forthcoming on QIP, dividend, and content-share ambitions. Repeatedly deferred specific numbers (PAT margin, MRO TAM, order sizes) and invited analysts to factory visits. Confident, partnership-led narrative around Fortune/global customers and Boeing endorsement (level-loading schedules).
non-obvious:
- Strategic agreements (~INR3,000cr) are OVER AND ABOVE the INR715cr confirmed POs — large under-appreciated visibility layer.
- Space customer is now Amazon (Kuiper), explicitly NOT Blue Origin anymore — a customer swap.
- New semiconductor customer being onboarded is "one of the largest semiconductor manufacturers in the world" (contract imminent) — second major semi anchor.
- Commercial aerospace: OEMs building India supply base have shortlisted Rossell; RFPs expected ~Q2 FY27 — order sizes "much larger" than defence/space/semi; potentially "transformational."
- Phase-2 (2028–29): move up value chain from harnesses/panels to electromechanical integrated systems & assemblies → margin 21–30%; content per platform "X into 3 to 5."
- Capex strategy reversed: leasing 210k sq ft instead of building — faster, capital-light.
- EPA clauses, advance payments and back-to-back supplier contracts newly built into agreements to de-risk RM/working capital.
- US RTI subsidiary being pushed by a space customer to expand — could anchor US space scale-up.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Presented as a globally recognised manufacturer of electrical wire harnesses and interconnect systems (EWIS) with a Fortune 500 client base, grown from a single customer at inception in 2011 to 30+ marquee customers across sectors.
- Moat framed as qualification and execution barriers — ITAR, AS9100D and NADCAP across 40 processes with multi-year qualification cycles — plus 8-12 year global OEM partnerships that the deck argues a new entrant cannot replicate.
- Claims deep embedding in decade-long global defence programs where switching costs are extremely high once a supplier is qualified.
- Growth is characterised as structural rather than cyclical, driven by defence budgets, commercial aerospace ramp-up, the global semiconductor mission and space liberalisation across four high-barrier industries.
- Customer validation is evidenced by Boeing Supplier of the Year (2015, 2019) and Performance Excellence awards, Honeywell Supplier Excellence (2023, 2024) and a BAE Systems Special Recognition Award (2025).

- FY27 revenue mix: ~50% aerospace & defence / ~50% non-A&D (space + semiconductor).
- Space + semiconductor each guided +300–400% YoY in FY27 (base: ~20% of FY26 revenue came from these two combined).
- EBITDA margin: structural 17–22% in current competencies; FY27 expected to improve vs FY26; MRO higher (services); phase-2 electromechanical assemblies (2028–29) could reach 21–30%.
- Semiconductor revenue potential ~US$200m in 3–5 years; T-7 strategic agreement ~US$200m.
- Inventory coverage targeted down from 7.67 months toward an eventual 4 months.
- Employee cost targeted below 15.5% of revenue.

growth_optionality.title: Growth
growth_optionality.body: Macro tailwinds: global commercial-aero production ramp, rising defence GDP spend, LEO/space ecosystem build-out, semiconductor-equipment capex with China+1 supply-base diversification into India, and supply-chain-resilience demand for "trusted manufacturing partners." Company-specific: high qualification barriers (moat), 300–400% growth in space & semi, content-share expansion ("X into 3 to 5") on existing platforms (phase-2, 2028+), commercial aerospace entry, MRO, and RTI US expansion. 98% of revenue exported (~80% North America; diversifying into Southeast Asia, Middle East, Europe).

margins.title: Margins
margins.body: FY26 EBITDA ~13.6% (INR66cr on INR485cr), below mgmt's 17–22% structural band and sequentially weaker — repeatedly questioned by analysts. Cause: front-loaded investment in people, infrastructure, training, tooling, automation, and heavy first-article-inspection (FAI)/qualification spend for new space & semiconductor customers that generates no current-year revenue but drives repeat orders and higher margins later. Mgmt insists margins improve in FY27 and that semiconductor (despite high-volume) stays in the 17–22% band via automation. Back-to-back supplier contracts + EPA (equitable price adjustment) clauses + advance/upfront payments on long-lead single-source items mitigate raw-material and working-capital risk.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Maiden dividend announced (quantum not specified on call). Planned QIP to raise ~7–10% (sized off market cap, 5% up/down band) — proceeds for (1) capacity expansion/facility footprint, (2) operational/quality/testing infrastructure, (3) working capital for scale & long-lead inventory; seeking "the right investor." Debt has risen with growth; multi-banking framework; additional working-capital facilities secured in Q4. Inventory-coverage reduction (7.67→4 months target) is the key self-funding lever. CFO acknowledged operating cash flow still negative, improvement expected over coming years.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Very bullish and promotional — "strongest quarter in history," "structurally higher growth trajectory," "sky's the limit," "designed to compound." MD candid on margin miss (attributes to investment/qualification, promises recovery) and forthcoming on QIP, dividend, and content-share ambitions. Repeatedly deferred specific numbers (PAT margin, MRO TAM, order sizes) and invited analysts to factory visits. Confident, partnership-led narrative around Fortune/global customers and Boeing endorsement (level-loading schedules).

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- Margins running below the 17–22% guide; recovery hinges on qualifications converting to repeat volume.
- Negative operating cash flow and rising debt while scaling ~90%/yr — heavy working-capital intensity.
- Execution-dilutive QIP (7–10% dilution) and dependence on raising capital to fund growth.
- Customer concentration: Boeing in A&D, single large customer in each of space (Amazon) and semiconductor today.
- Legacy loss-making Boeing program (~INR70cr) still to run off in H1 FY27.
- Revenue 98% export / ~80% North America → FX, US tariff/policy and freight exposure (though customers pay freight, air-freighted, mostly CIF/customer-paid).
- Guidance is qualitative ("similar to last year"); space/semi 300–400% growth off a small base; commercial-aero entry still pre-RFP.
- Margin pressure if semiconductor volume mix dilutes blended profitability.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- Strategic agreements (~INR3,000cr) are OVER AND ABOVE the INR715cr confirmed POs — large under-appreciated visibility layer.
- Space customer is now Amazon (Kuiper), explicitly NOT Blue Origin anymore — a customer swap.
- New semiconductor customer being onboarded is "one of the largest semiconductor manufacturers in the world" (contract imminent) — second major semi anchor.
- Commercial aerospace: OEMs building India supply base have shortlisted Rossell; RFPs expected ~Q2 FY27 — order sizes "much larger" than defence/space/semi; potentially "transformational."
- Phase-2 (2028–29): move up value chain from harnesses/panels to electromechanical integrated systems & assemblies → margin 21–30%; content per platform "X into 3 to 5."
- Capex strategy reversed: leasing 210k sq ft instead of building — faster, capital-light.
- EPA clauses, advance payments and back-to-back supplier contracts newly built into agreements to de-risk RM/working capital.
- US RTI subsidiary being pushed by a space customer to expand — could anchor US space scale-up.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
First tracked file for ROSSTECH (no prior summary in repo). Key Q4 FY26 / FY26 markers from this call:
- Record Q4 revenue ~INR142cr (+62% YoY); FY26 revenue INR485cr (+87% YoY); PBT INR10cr→INR28cr; EBITDA INR38cr→INR66cr.
- FY26 EBITDA margin ~13.6% — below 17–22% structural guide and sequentially weaker; attributed to qualification/FAI and investment spend.
- Confirmed POs ~INR715cr; strategic agreements ~INR3,000cr clarified as OVER AND ABOVE POs; FY26 bids ~INR4,500cr.
- New disclosures: ~INR400cr multi-year space win; T-7 ~US$200m; space customer is Amazon (not Blue Origin); new top-tier semiconductor customer being onboarded; semi+space each guided +300–400% FY27.
- Capex pivot: leasing ~210,000 sq ft adjacent facility instead of building new.
- Capital actions: maiden dividend declared; QIP planned (~7–10% dilution); inventory coverage 10→7.67 months, targeting 4; employee cost 15.5% of revenue.
- New markets/licenses: DPL + AS9110 MRO licenses obtained; commercial-aero RFPs expected ~Q2 FY27; US RTI expansion under evaluation.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] Demerged from Rossell India Ltd and relisted as Rossell Techsys Ltd in December 2024; a Rossell India senior finance executive continues on the board as a non-executive director.
- [Board] Board includes former HAL Chairman & MD Talari Suvarna Raju and former Secretary (Defense Finance) Shobhana Joshi, giving direct defence-procurement and policy access alongside promoter directors Harsh Mohan Gupta and Rishab Mohan Gupta.
- [Certification] ITAR certification and a pending CMMC V2.0 push are regulatory prerequisites for US defence work and effectively gate the addressable customer set.
